questions.q: What is the recommended order for presenting this capstone project, according to this lesson?
options: Lineage graph, then the docs site, then test coverage, then a passing CI run, then the snapshot's history, then the Power BI report
Show the Power BI report first and nothing else
Read the raw source files row by row
There is no recommended order — present however feels natural
questions.explain: The lesson lays out a specific six-step walkthrough that builds from foundational lineage up to the connected report, each step proving a specific claim with real evidence.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say fct_orders joins on a surrogate key rather than the customer's natural ID?
options: A natural-key join can't survive a customer's segment changing without losing the old value — the surrogate key is what makes SCD Type 2 history possible
Surrogate keys are required by dbt for every model with no other reason
Natural keys are not allowed to exist in a dbt project
There is no real difference between the two approaches
questions.explain: This is a direct callback to the snapshot-backed dimension from Lesson 43 — the surrogate key indirection is what preserves history.

questions.q: According to this lesson, how should you demonstrate that your singular test is real, not just declared?
options: Run dbt test live and be ready to explain what the specific rule your singular test protects against
Describe it verbally with no supporting evidence
Show a screenshot of the test file being written
Skip discussing tests entirely during a presentation
questions.explain: The lesson emphasizes running dbt test live and explaining what the singular test actually protects against, not just that generic tests exist.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what course(s) can follow this one in the Analytics Engineer path?
options: Git, GitHub & CI/CD for Data, and/or the Advanced stage with Azure Data Factory and Apache Airflow
There is nothing after this course in the entire catalog
A second, unrelated dbt course covering the exact same material
Only a course on Oracle Financial Applications
questions.explain: The lesson names both directions explicitly: the Git/GitHub/CI-CD course (which reuses this exact project) and the Advanced stage's Data Factory/Airflow courses.

questions.q: What does this final lesson say actually transfers to any transformation tool at any company, regardless of dbt-specific syntax?
options: The discipline of version control, testing, documentation, and a generated (not hand-drawn) lineage graph
The exact YAML syntax used in this specific project
Nothing from this course transfers to other tools
Only the specific Snowflake SQL used in the marts models
questions.explain: The lesson states explicitly that the discipline — not any one tool's specific syntax — is what carries forward.
